records.name: Naive vs Timezone-Aware Datetime Semantics

interpretation.description: Naive datetime holds year, month, day, hour, minute, second without offset or timezone context. Aware datetime includes timezone offset or IANA zone.
interpretation.python_behavior: Comparing naive and aware datetime raises TypeError. Converting naive to aware requires explicit tzinfo assignment or zoneinfo.ZoneInfo.
interpretation.sas_behavior: Standard SAS datetime values are wall-clock naive. SAS E8601DX format parses ISO offsets, but native numeric values have no tz attribute.

ambiguity.reason: Naive datetimes cannot be compared across different locales or converted accurately across DST boundaries.

records.canonical_representation: UTC timestamp with explicit 'Z' or offset
validation_rules: Never perform arithmetic between naive and aware timestamps
Migration from SAS to Python must explicitly declare whether wall-clock naive or UTC-aware is intended

records.name: Daylight Saving Transitions (Spring Gap and Autumn Fold)

interpretation.description: During spring forward, local time jumps (non-existent hour). During autumn back, local time repeats (ambiguous hour).
interpretation.python_behavior: PEP 495 introduced fold attribute (fold=0 for first occurrence, fold=1 for repeated occurrence).
interpretation.sql_behavior: PostgreSQL AT TIME ZONE resolves repeated time to standard time by default.

ambiguity.reason: Times falling in repeated fold hour require explicit disambiguation flag.

validation_rules: Store UTC internally to avoid ambiguity during DST transitions

interpretation.description: Offset format [+-]HH:mm or [+-]HHmm or Z. 'Z' is equivalent to +00:00 (Zulu / UTC).
interpretation.gotchas: Offsets represent instantaneous difference from UTC at a single moment; they do not represent geographic zones with seasonal DST rules.
